objectives.d1: Find Finch on the upper terrace. Take the steps north of the square.
objectives.d1b: Smoke is stuck. Stand near him and sing (Q).
objectives.d2: Meet Finch in the brood caves, east of the lower terrace by the spring.
objectives.d3: It's evening. Corran has gone up on the drying-house roof. Climb the ladder.
objectives.d4: Go home to sleep. Your house is the north-west door.
objectives.n1: Nine days later. Something is wrong in the square.
objectives.n2: Corran is back from Millbridge. He's waiting at your house.
objectives.n3: Meet Tamsin at the south gate and take the greenling run.
objectives.n3b: Follow the trail down the mountain.
objectives.n4: The sky above the cloud is orange. Climb back to Larkfold.
objectives.n5: Someone is alive in the square.
objectives.i1b: Six months later. The pressure bell is ringing. Go through the hatchery door.
objectives.i2: Find Finch in the steam and get him out.
objectives.i4: A fresh lull in a tin on the table. Finch is in the next room.
objectives.d0: Maren is waiting by the warm spring, east of the lower terrace. Someone has come up the mountain.
objectives.d2b: Corran and Tamsin are loading the market panniers by the south gate.
objectives.n2b: You wake. Corran's side of the bed is cold. Find him.
objectives.n2d: Morning. Maren wants a word in the square.
objectives.n2e: Go home and rest. The greenling run is in two nights.
objectives.n5c: Climb to the top terrace, where Finch tried to call Smoke down.
objectives.c1: Lead the column up the cloud path. At the last cairn, give the signal.
objectives.c2: Go up to the cloud gate.

talk.text: "Corran carried the last run down himself. Says the Millbridge market likes his face better than mine. Can't think why."
"Your mother used to sing at the trays too. Said the larvae grew calmer for it. Nonsense, of course. I miss it."
"I'm cutting moss for Finch's trays. He says if I cut it too thick the lulls bite harder. Is that true?"
"Three hundred in Millbridge on our greenlings now. Your mother would be proud. Mind the measures."
The foal stamps and looks at the sky. He won't come for a voice he doesn't know.
"Eleven. All on the last brood. They went to sleep and didn't wake up."
Ash, the old pack loftbuck, chews his lead and waits for the panniers.

else.text: Finch looks at you and says nothing at all.

talk.text: A Larkfold girl of seven, crying without making any sound.
A Larkfold child. They won't look at you.
A Larkfold child. They won't look at you.
You get him over your shoulder. Your back takes the steam.
Mother's notes: "Wild lulls bite to keep their host still. The bite numbs. That is all a lull is: a mouth that doesn't want to be scratched off."
Mother's notes: "The Guild lines are sterile. Two parent lines, kept in the Broodhouse in Vantry. Every Guild lull in Ostrel is a child of those two. Nobody else can breed them."
Mother's notes: "The larvae eat only duskwort. More moss, bigger glands, stronger bite. Measure the moss and you measure the medicine."
Mother's notes: "Step a person down one strength each fortnight. Too fast and they go into the raw. Too strong a brood and the heart slows. Never guess a measure."

do.fade: Dr Lisle's surgery, the next morning.

do.toast: Not yet. Finch is in the next bed.

do.text: Grey larvae the size of rice grains, feeding on chopped duskwort. In a season they'll be greenlings.
The brood book. Tonight's measures in Finch's careful, enormous letters, and Pell's cramped ones on the moss column. Every line matches your mother's table.
The spring is warm as a bath. That warmth is why Larkfold exists, and why it's hidden.
Smoke from the terraces drifts out over the cloud.
Cloud, all the way down. Somewhere under it are the lowlands, the mills, and Millbridge.
An indenture cart. The children inside have been sorted by height.
A coal boiler, hissing.

do.toast: Smoke can't hear you from here. Get closer.
Not here. Climb to the top terrace.

then.text: "Smoke's stuck at the far end and he won't come for me. Rhea, he won't listen to me."

then.choose: Smoke is at the east end of the terrace, refusing to move.

options.label: "I'll sing for him."
options.hint: The foal song. You sang it to him every night after he was born.

options.label: "Try once more. Whistle, don't shout."
options.hint: He has to learn it himself.

do.text: Finch whistles. Smoke looks at the sky. Finch looks at you.
"Fine. You sing, then."

smokeComes.text: Three notes and the foal comes clattering across the terrace, nearly knocking you flat, and pushes his head into your hip.
"It's always the song. Teach me it properly. I'm on the trays tonight, come down to the caves."
"He still knows your voice. He was a day old when you first sang it to him. Kith never forget whoever sang to them first."

finchCaves.choose: The brood book is open on the bench. These trays go down to Millbridge next month, where Corran's mother and sister are weaning.

options.label: Check his measures
options.hint: It's his first season on the trays.

do.text: Every line in the book matches your mother's table. He watches you check and says nothing, and you feel slightly foolish.

options.label: Leave him to it
options.hint: He'll never learn if you hover.

do.text: "Thank you."
He's humming the foal song under his breath, badly.

evening.toast: Smoke goes home with Finch. Evening falls.

then.text: Corran is lying on the warm tiles, watching the stars come out over the cloud.
"Three years married, and I still wake some nights thinking I'm back in a Guild barracks, in a grey coat, waiting for the bugle."
"Eight years since I was a Warden. You'd think it would wear off."

do.text: "Hask. A village on the far ridge, caught with a brood room. We hanged the adults in the square and put the children on carts. I walked away the next morning and didn't stop until I saw your terraces."
"Second month on greenlings. My sister says she sleeps through the night now. First time in years."
"Most nights I can't believe they let me stay. Then you sing at the trays and I stop wondering."

else.text: It's the middle of the day.

news.text: "Eleven people weaning on our last brood went to sleep in Millbridge and didn't wake. Their hearts slowed and stopped. Corran's mother and his sister are two of them."
"He's gone down to bury them. Took the brood book with him."
"Guild agents. They tampered with the trays on the road. It's what they do."

news.choose: The square goes quiet, waiting for you, because it was your mother's recipe.

options.label: Believe the elders
options.hint: They raised you. The Guild has done worse.

options.label: Ask whether anyone checked the brood book
options.hint: A brood can come out too strong.

do.text: "It went to Millbridge with Corran. When he's back, ask him. Not before."

afterNews.toast: Two days pass. Corran comes home.

beg.text: Corran comes back from the burial grey and soaked through, and doesn't take his coat off.

then.text: "I read the brood book on the road. Every measure is your mother's. Whatever killed them, it wasn't the numbers."

beg.text: "My old captain found me at the grave. Halloran. He says a Warden column has traced the greenlings up the mountain. They'll be here before the snows. Same orders as Hask."

then.text: "You know what Hask was. I told you on the roof. Take Finch. We go tonight, over the passes into Lorne. The Guild has no say in Lorne. Please."

else.text: "I was at Hask, Rhea. They hanged the adults in the square and put the children on carts. Take Finch. We go tonight, over the passes into Lorne. The Guild has no say in Lorne. Please."

beg.choose: Rhea won't leave. How does she refuse?

options.label: "Three hundred people are weaning on our greenlings."
options.hint: If Larkfold goes, they go into the raw with nothing.

options.label: "You'd trust a Warden captain over our elders?"
options.hint: Cold, and he hears every word.

options.label: "This is our home. Stay and help us move the brood."
options.hint: Ask him to fight for it with you.

refused.text: He doesn't argue. That's the worst of it. He sits by the fire with his coat still on until you fall asleep.

tamsinGate.text: "Panniers are loaded. Maren weighed every tray herself this time. The three hundred can't skip a fortnight, whatever happened. Ash knows the trail. Quiet night for it."

trailFight.text: Grey coats on the trail. Wardens, holding the path, with a reedcat on a chain.

win.text: Below you the trail is empty. Above you, the top of the cloud has gone orange, where Larkfold should be.
You drop the panniers and climb.

burned.text: By dawn there is nothing to climb to. The terraces are black. Every child under fourteen is gone. Finch is gone. Smoke is gone. Corran is gone.
The elders are on the drying-house beam. You don't look twice.
Somewhere in the square, someone is calling your name.

ashTerrace.text: The top terrace. Hoofprints in the ash where Smoke stamped and refused to come down, a fortnight and a lifetime ago.

options.label: Sing the foal song
options.hint: The one he always came to.

options.label: Not yet
options.hint: Walk the terrace first. Sing (Q) when you're ready.

singAsh.text: You sit where Finch tried to call the foal down, and you sing the first verse, because you don't know what else to do.

interlude.text: You're standing in a yard in Vantry, beside the carts. Your head still rings. Every child from Larkfold is here, sorted by height.

then.text: "You've nothing to buy a child with, Dace. But I need a man on the hatchery night watch. Nobody wants it. Take it, and I'll sign one indenture over to your household. The child still works the hatchery, but on the clerk's side, out of the brood rooms, under your eye."

then.choose: Finch is by the second cart, looking straight at you. By the last cart, a girl of seven called Sela is crying without making a sound.

options.label: Take the watch. Ask for Finch.
options.hint: The one you promised to protect.

options.label: Take the vat-cleaning duty too. Ask for Finch, and for Sela to be kept out of the brood rooms.
options.hint: A second post nobody wants. You'll sleep even less.

else.text: "Night watch starts at dusk, Dace. Don't be late."

then.text: He laughs and signs Finch's paper over to you. Then he writes against the girl's number.
"Sorting house, not brood. She'll count trays and copy ledgers. Nobody puts her in a breeding room."

afterCarts.text: There is no answer to that. From now on he calls you Warden, and nothing else.

enterHatchery.fade: Six months later. House Mire's hatchery, the night watch.

enterHatchery.text: Brood rooms are kept hot and wet by coal boilers, because larvae die in the cold. The pressure bell is ringing. Steam is pouring out of all four boilers.
Finch works on the clerk's side, far end, east wall. Steam burns. Don't stand in it long.

hatcheryFail.text: You go down on your knees in the white. Someone drags you out by the collar.

then.text: Your back and both hands are scalded raw. Finch has a burn on one arm. The pain is so complete you can't sleep, can't hold a cup, can't think.
"House line or field line. The house line will take it all away. The field line takes the edge off. Set at the back of the neck, it reaches the spine."

then.choose: In the tin, on damp moss, two grey lulls the size of a thumbnail.

options.label: The house line
options.hint: Take it all away.

options.label: The field line
options.hint: Bear what it doesn't touch.

later.fade: A month later. The burns have healed. The lull has died and dropped off, leaving a small round scar.

then.text: For a month you felt nothing. Not the burns, not your mother, not the carts.

else.text: For a month the burns were a dull ache instead of a scream. Some nights you still lay awake thinking about the carts.

later.text: Lisle sent a fresh one round anyway, in a tin, for the evenings. Evenings are when you think about Rhea. You promised Finch you'd teach him the Guild ledgers tonight. He's in the next room.

then.choose: The tin is cool in your hand. Something moves inside it.

options.label: Put the fresh lull on
options.hint: Just for the evenings.

do.text: The bite is a cold pinch at the back of your neck, then nothing at all. Much later, you notice Finch knocked twice and stopped.

options.label: Leave it
options.hint: Walk away from the table.

then.text: Your hands shake on the ledger page, and the raw keeps you up until dawn. Finch doesn't say anything, but he stays until the last line.

pilgrimFit.text: A woman sits on the rim of the warm spring with her boots off, a strip of dark cloth in her lap. Eight small round scars climb the side of her neck, one above the other.
"Rhea, this is Hessa, from Millbridge. Tamsin brought her up last night."
"With that over my eyes for the last mile. So you're the doctor. Where am I?"

pilgrimFit.choose: Hessa wants to know where she is.

options.label: "Larkfold. Come and look over the wall."

do.text: Below the terrace wall there is nothing but cloud, white and flat, all the way to the edge of the sky.
"We're above the clouds. In Millbridge they say there's nothing up the mountain but rock."
"Good. Let them keep saying it."

options.label: "Somewhere safe. Better you don't know more."

do.text: "The blindfold, and now this. You're careful people."
"We have to be. She's in Larkfold, Rhea, she can know that much. She just can't ever find the way back."

pilgrimFit.text: "Let me see your neck. Eight rings. Eight months?"

"One ring for every lull. You buy one at the Guild shop, it bites on, and for a month there's no pain at all. My back's been broken since the mill. Then it dies and drops off and leaves its ring, and in a day the raw comes."
"Shaking. Sweating. Every nerve on fire, for days. So you go back to the shop, and the price has gone up again. It always goes up."
"So she came to us. Rhea, fetch a third strength from the warm trays and show her."
You lift a greenling from the moss with two fingers. It's the size of a thumbnail, grey-green, and it curls towards the warmth of your hand.
"It's a greenling. We breed them here, in the warm caves, and each strength is weaker than the last. Every fortnight you step down one strength, until you don't need one at all. No raw."

pilgrimFit.choose: Hessa looks at the greenling, then at you.

options.label: "It won't hurt. It numbs the place it bites, that's all."
options.hint: Gentle.

do.text: "That's what the Guild man said about the first one."
But she turns her head and lets you set it.

options.label: "The first fortnight will still be hard. I won't lie to you."
options.hint: Honest.

do.text: "Nobody's ever told me that before. Go on, then."

pilgrimFit.text: The greenling settles at the back of her neck. Her shoulders come down slowly, like a held breath let go.
"If it's that simple, why has the Guild never done it?"
"Because then nobody would need the Guild shop. Breeding lulls without a Guild licence is a hanging matter. Three hundred people in Millbridge are on our greenlings now."
"Hanging. Who'd come all the way up here to hang you?"
"Wardens. The Guild's soldiers, in grey coats. That's why you came up blindfolded, and why only Larkfold folk ever walk the cloud path."
"Now go and find your brother, Rhea. Finch has been shouting for you all morning."

panniers.text: Panniers of greenling trays stand by the south gate, packed in warm wet moss for the trip down. Corran and Tamsin are roping them onto the frames.
"Fortnight run. Three hundred greenlings for Millbridge, and two of them for Corran's mother and sister."
"Second month. My sister wrote. She says Ma laughs again."

Finch has slipped out of the caves to watch. Corran crouches beside him and points past the drying house, where the moss for the trays hangs in long racks, to the north edge of the village, where the cloud lies thick against the cliff.
"See the cairns, going down into the cloud? Little stacks of three stones. That's the cloud path. In fog you walk cairn to cairn, and you never step off."
"Can you walk it in the dark?"
"With a lamp. Coming home late, you stop at the last cairn and blink the lamp three times, so the gate watch knows it's a friend. Three blinks. Larkfold folk only."
He says it over to himself, blinking at nothing.
"And if you ever tell anyone outside the valley, I'll throw you off it myself. Go on, the pair of you. It's nearly dark."

gateLie.text: Corran is at the south gate on his own, with a shuttered lamp. He's turning something over in his fingers. When he hears you, he closes his hand.
"Corran? It's the middle of the night."
"Couldn't sleep. I keep seeing the graves."
You've seen what's in his hand before, in the pocket of his old coat: a disc of grey horn on a cord, with the Guild's lantern cut into it. Wardens carry them.
"From an old friend. A long time ago. I came out here to throw it off the cliff."

options.label: "What old friend? Halloran?"
options.hint: Press him.

do.text: "...Halloran wants me back. He says there's still a place for me. I told him no."
It's the first time he's ever looked away from you while he talks.

options.label: Take his hand and bring him back to bed
options.hint: Let it go. He's grieving.

do.text: He lets you lead him. The token goes into his pocket, not off the cliff.

gateLie.text: "Go back to bed, Rhea. I'll be in in a minute."

knot.text: Corran has been up since before dawn. He's fixed the drying-house shutters and carried water for Oda, and now he's sitting in the dust with Finch, teaching him a knot.
"Over, under, back through. It's a Warden's knot. Holds a loftbuck, holds a cart, and it comes free with one pull if you know where."
He looks up at you and smiles, and for a moment he's the man who came up the cloud path three years ago.

swappedRun.text: "Your husband came to me this morning. He wants you on the greenling run with Tamsin in two nights, instead of him."
"He says he can't face the Millbridge market so soon after the funeral, and you could do with a night off the mountain. He's been kind to everyone all day. Grief takes people strangely."

signal.text: Halfway down, Tamsin stops dead and catches your sleeve.
"Look. Over there, on the north cliff."
Far across the valley, where the cloud path climbs the cliff, a lamp blinks in the dark. Once. Twice. Three times. Then it goes out.
"That's ours. That's the friend signal. Who's coming up the cloud path at this hour?"

signal.choose: Rhea stares at where the lamp was.

do.text: "...Yes. A runner. Come on."
"Neither do I. I don't like it."

rookDying.text: Old Rook is sitting against the flagpole with his hands folded over his stomach. There's a lot of blood. He's very calm.
"They didn't come up the trail. They came out of the cloud, by the cloud gate, quiet as you like. Davin opened it for them. He thought it was a friend."
"Corran was at the front, with a lamp. Walking the lanes, calling, stay inside, stay inside, nobody will be hurt. I think he believed it. Right up until the torches."

do.text: "I'm sorry, girl. I saw his face."
His hand is already cold. He squeezes once.

rookDying.text: "Look after the songs. Somebody has to."
Then he's gone, and the square is very quiet.

ringNote.text: Your house is still standing. On the shelf by the bed, where he always leaves his things, is Corran's wedding ring, with a scrap torn from the brood book under it.
One line, in his handwriting: "They promised me. I'm sorry."
You thread the ring onto a cord and put it round your neck. You don't know why.

cloudPath.text: You know every cairn on the cloud path. You've walked it a hundred times, and taught it to Finch. You never thought you'd walk it with a column of Wardens at your back.
"No hangings. No burning. No children on carts. We go in quiet, we take the brood, we take the elders down to Vantry to answer for it. An arrest, Dace. Not Hask."
"And your wife's down the trail with the greenlings, where you sent her. She won't see any of it."

giveSignal.text: The last cairn. Above you, the dark shape of the cloud gate, and one lamp burning behind it.

do.text: "Every hour you stand here, Dace, someone in Millbridge goes into the raw. Or a column comes up the hard way, with torches from the start."
You lift the lamp.

cloudGate.text: "Corran? That's the friend signal. Who've you got with you?"

cloudGate.choose: Davin has kept the cloud gate for twenty years.

options.label: "Traders from Lorne. Open up, Davin, it's freezing."

do.text: "At this hour? ...Go on, then."

options.label: "Davin. Trust me. Open the gate. Nobody will be hurt."

do.text: "Nobody will be...? Corran, what is this?"
But he opens it. He's known you three years.

cloudGate.text: The gate swings in. The column goes past you into Larkfold, quiet as snow.
For a while it's what Halloran promised. Doors knocked on. Names read out. You walk the lanes with your lamp, calling: stay inside, stay inside, nobody will be hurt.
Then Halloran looks at the drying house, and the terraces, and the brood caves, and says one word.
"You gave me your word! Halloran, you gave me your word!"
Something hits the back of your head. The last thing you see is the drying house catching, and the thatch going up like paper.

cloudGate.fade: Four days later. Vantry, the Guild's city.

opening.text: "Rhea! Down here, by the warm spring. Somebody's come up the mountain in the night, and she needs the doctor."

opening.toast: Walk with the arrow keys or WASD, hold Shift to run, and press Enter to talk. Your goal is at the top left.
